taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and ITIS; Texas is within the native range, but the project currently has only one exact target-zone county.
look_here_first: Check the stem before the fruit: branchlets are uniformly red to purplish-red or chestnut, while leaves are usually deeply 3–5-lobed with long-pointed lobes and nearly glabrous undersides.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis is supported by a physical herbarium specimen. Broader Texas nativity is not converted into Hays or other nearby county records.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification. Preserve the one-county HOLD.

best_field_traits: branchlets uniformly red, purplish-red, or chestnut
branchlets glabrous or only sparsely cobwebby
leaves usually deeply 3–5-lobed with long-acuminate tips
leaf undersides glabrous or nearly so
berries blue-black to black, roughly 8–10 mm
riverbank, slough, and alluvial floodplain habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The combination of red stems, deep lobing, and nearly glabrous lower leaf surfaces separates it from the hairier V. cinerea and more glaucous-fruited V. berlandieri.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Uniform red branchlets + deeply lobed leaves + glabrous lower surface are the fastest field combination.
